newsitem.title: CANADA: Bank of Canada cuts bank rate 25 points to 3.25 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Canada cuts bank rate 25 points to 3.25 pct.

text.p: The Bank of Canada cut its key bank rate by 25 basis points to 3.25 percent by intervening in the money market on Friday, money market traders said.

The move effectively lowered the central bank's target range for the call loan or overnight lending rate to 2.75-3.25 from 3.0-3.5 percent. The bank rate is the top of the central bank's target range for the overnight rate and is the rate at which it lends to financial institutions in its role as lender of last resort. A basis point is one-hundredth of a percentage point.

The Bank of Canada said in a news release after the cut that the move was to offset the tightening impact on monetary conditions of a stronger Canadian dollar. The bank also said the move ratified the recent decline in short-term market interest rates.

It was the 11th rate cut this year by the Bank of Canada and the 10th independent of a cut by the U.S. Federal Reserve. The Bank of Canada has now cut rates by a total of 500 basis points, or a half a percentage point, since May 1995.
The latest rate cut brought the bank rate, which has changed in nature over the years, to its lowest level since December 1961.
Canadian financial markets traded steady after the cut.
